title: Proposal for Redacted Version of Banned Book "Red Lines: Political Cartoons and the Struggle Against Censorship" to be Considered for Publication
what_it_is: Proposal for Redacted Version of Banned Book "Red Lines: Political Cartoons and the Struggle Against Censorship" to be Considered for Publication

sections.label: Red Lines book objectionable
sections.summary: IMDA assessed "Red Lines" as objectionable under the Undesirable Publications Act because it contains images denigrating religions, including Charlie Hebdo's cartoons of Prophet Muhammad.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) has assessed the publication "Red Lines: Political Cartoons and the Struggle Against Censorship" to be objectionable under the Undesirable Publications Act (UPA) as the book contains images that denigrate religions, including the reproduction of Charlie Hebdo’s cartoons of Prophet Muhammad.

sections.label: Six other objectionable publications
sections.summary: IMDA assessed six other publications as objectionable for denigrating religious communities, and removal of offensive content would not automatically allow distribution.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In the last five years, IMDA has assessed six other publications, besides "Red Lines", to be objectionable for denigrating various religious communities.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For example, in 2020, IMDA deemed the book "Understanding the Evil of Innovation" objectionable as the book contained strong denigratory references towards Judaism and Christianity.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Removal of the offensive content will not automatically lead to these publications being allowed for distribution.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Revised versions would have to be re-assessed holistically and none of the publishers have sought to do so.  "Red Lines" was launched in the United States of America on 31 August 2021, before IMDA took a decision on its suitability for distribution in Singapore.

sections.label: Objectionable publications distribution penalties
sections.summary: Publishers can ask IMDA to assess revised versions, IMDA keeps a database, and importing, selling, distributing, making or reproducing objectionable publications is an offence.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If and when they do so, they can approach IMDA to assess the suitability of a revised version of "Red Lines" for distribution in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To ensure that publications which have been deemed objectionable are not distributed in Singapore, IMDA maintains a database of these publications which importers and book distributors can refer to.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It is an offence for any person to import, sell, distribute, make or reproduce an objectionable publication.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The penalty is a fine not exceeding $5,000 or jail not exceeding 12 months or both.
